2026-08-19.content:
[Global Front End](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/networking/cross-cloud-network/global-front-end/gfee-overview)
is a unified offering that simplifies billing by consolidating pricing across
networking products, including Cloud CDN,
global external Application Load Balancer, Google Cloud Armor, and Service Extensions,
into one solution to help deliver, scale, and secure your internet-facing
applications. Cloud CDN is included in the
Global Front End Enterprise billing tier. This feature is available in **Preview**.

For more information, see [Global Front End](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/overview#cdn_with_globalfrontend).

summary.title: Unified Global Front End for Network Services
summary.summary: Introducing Global Front End, a new offering that simplifies billing for networking products like Cloud CDN and external Application Load Balancer. This unified solution helps deliver, scale, and secure your internet-facing applications. It is currently available in Preview.

2026-08-17.content:
Cloud CDN supports the targeted `CDN-Cache-Control` HTTP response
header [RFC 9213](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9213). You can use
this header to specify caching directives specifically for Cloud CDN edge
caches without affecting browser-level caching.

For details, see [Cache control header precedence](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/caching#cache-control-headers).

summary.title: Cloud CDN supports targeted cache control
summary.summary: Cloud CDN now supports the CDN-Cache-Control HTTP header, allowing for specific caching directives for edge caches without impacting browser caching. This feature enhances cache management flexibility.

2026-08-04.content:
Cloud CDN supports native image optimization at the Google network edge
for global external Application Load Balancers. This feature offloads
compute-intensive image transformations, such as resizing, cropping,
and format conversion to reduce origin server load and egress costs.
This feature is in **Preview**.

**Note:** During the Preview phase, image optimization is available free of charge.
Charges will apply once it becomes Generally Available (GA).

For more information, see [Optimize images with Cloud CDN](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/imageoptimization).

summary.title: Edge Image Optimization with Cloud CDN
summary.summary: Cloud CDN now offers native image optimization at the network edge for global external Application Load Balancers. This feature reduces origin server load and egress costs by performing image transformations like resizing and format conversion directly on the network. This capability is currently in Preview and is available at no charge during this phase.

2026-07-03.content:
Cloud CDN and external Application Load Balancers support self-service
Private Bucket Access for Cloud Storage buckets. This feature allows you to
securely serve content without making your storage buckets public. The access
on the buckets is managed securely via IAM permissions on a Google-managed
service account. This feature is **Generally Available**.

For more information, see [Private bucket access](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/setting-up-cdn-with-bucket#enable_private_bucket_access).

summary.title: Securely Serve Cloud Storage Content
summary.summary: Cloud CDN and external Application Load Balancers now support self-service Private Bucket Access for Cloud Storage. This allows you to securely serve content without making buckets public, managing access through IAM permissions. This feature is now Generally Available.

2026-06-25.content:
Cloud CDN and external Application Load Balancers support self-service
Private Bucket Access for Cloud Storage buckets. This feature allows you to
securely serve content without making your storage buckets public. The access
on the buckets is managed securely via IAM permissions on a Google-managed
service account. This feature is **Generally Available**.

For more information, see [Private bucket access](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/setting-up-cdn-with-bucket#enable_private_bucket_access).

summary.title: Securely serve content from Cloud Storage
summary.summary: Cloud CDN and external Application Load Balancers now support self-service Private Bucket Access for Cloud Storage. This feature allows you to securely serve content without making your storage buckets public, managing access through IAM permissions. This functionality is now Generally Available.

2026-05-26.content:
For [global external Application Load Balancers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https/setting-up-global-traffic-mgmt#cdn-cache-policy), you can configure Cloud CDN
cache policies at various levels of a URL map, providing more granular control
over caching. You can now apply specific caching logic based on hostnames,
URL paths, HTTP headers, and query parameters. This feature is
**Generally Available**.

For more information, see [Cache policies in URL maps](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/caching#cache-policies-url-maps).

summary.title: Granular Cloud CDN Cache Policies
summary.summary: Configure Cloud CDN cache policies with greater control using URL maps. Apply specific caching logic based on hostnames, paths, headers, and query parameters for enhanced performance. This feature is now Generally Available.

2026-04-30.content:
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Gateway supports Cloud CDN to help you cache
content closer to your users, improve application latency, and reduce origin
load. Using GKE Gateway APIs, you can configure, manage, and fine-tune caching
configurations for different segments of your traffic. This feature is **Generally Available**.

For more information, see [Configure Cloud CDN for Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-cdn-for-gateway).

summary.title: Cache content closer to users with GKE Gateway
summary.summary: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Gateway now supports Cloud CDN. This integration allows you to cache content closer to your users, improving application latency and reducing origin load. You can easily configure and manage caching settings for various traffic segments using GKE Gateway APIs.

2026-04-13.content:
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Gateway supports Cloud CDN to help you cache
content closer to your users, improve application latency, and reduce origin
load. Using GKE Gateway APIs, you can configure, manage, and fine-tune caching
configurations for different segments of your traffic. This feature is in **Preview**.

For more information, see [Configure Cloud CDN for Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/configure-cdn-for-gateway).

summary.title: GKE Gateway now supports Cloud CDN
summary.summary: GKE Gateway now integrates with Cloud CDN, enabling you to cache content closer to users. This feature aims to reduce latency and origin load, offering more control over caching configurations. This is a preview feature.

2026-03-30.content:
For [global external Application Load Balancers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https/setting-up-global-traffic-mgmt#cdn-cache-policy), you can configure Cloud CDN
cache policies at various levels of a URL map, providing more granular control
over caching. You can now apply specific caching logic based on hostnames,
URL paths, HTTP headers, and query parameters. This feature is in **Preview**.

For more information, see [Cache policies in URL maps](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/caching#cache-policies-url-maps).

summary.title: Granular Cloud CDN Cache Policies
summary.summary: Configure Cloud CDN cache policies at multiple levels within a URL map for more granular control. This feature allows specific caching logic based on hostnames, URL paths, headers, and query parameters. This is a preview feature.

2025-11-13.content: Cloud CDN lets you [add custom code to the request processing path](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/integration-with-service-extensions) of global external Application Load Balancers by using Service Extensions edge extensions (pre-cache) and traffic extensions (post-cache). These extensions help you manipulate request headers early in the processing lifecycle to influence caching and routing decisions. This feature is in **General Availability**.

summary.title: Cloud CDN Service Extensions
summary.summary: Use Service Extensions with Cloud CDN to customize request processing for caching and routing.

2025-10-07.content:
Cloud CDN provides predefined dashboards that are enabled by default for a quick
insight into system health and performance. These dashboards display key metrics
that enable you to monitor traffic distribution and cache effectiveness without
manual configuration. This feature is **Generally Available**.

For more information, see [Predefined dashboards](https://docs.cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/logging#predefined-cdn-dashboards).

summary.title: Cloud CDN Predefined Dashboards Now Available
summary.summary: Gain quick insights into your system's health and performance with Cloud CDN's new predefined dashboards. Monitor traffic distribution and cache effectiveness effortlessly with key metrics displayed by default, requiring no manual setup. This feature is Generally Available.

2025-06-23.content:
Cloud CDN lets you add custom code to the request processing path of global external Application Load Balancers by using Service Extensions edge extensions. These extensions help you implement customizations in the request path pre-cache, which can influence how content is cached and the backend service is selected on the Application Load Balancer. This feature is in **Preview**.

For more information, see [Use Service Extensions for edge computing](https://cloud.google.com/cdn/docs/integration-with-service-extensions).

summary.title: Cloud CDN introduces Service Extensions for custom request processing
summary.summary: You can now add custom code to the request processing path of global external Application Load Balancers using Service Extensions edge extensions. These extensions enable pre-cache customizations to influence content caching and backend selection. This feature is currently in Preview.
